sections.title: Introduction to Number Series
sections.content: Number Series is a sequence of numbers following a specific mathematical pattern. At Level 1, the goal is to identify basic mathematical operations like addition, subtraction, basic multiplication, squares, cubes, or prime numbers to find the missing term.

sections.title: Difference Series (Addition/Subtraction)
sections.content: The most common and basic pattern. The difference between consecutive terms is constant, or it follows a simple arithmetic progression. Always start by calculating the difference between adjacent terms.

sections.title: Prime Number Series
sections.content: The series consists exclusively of prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17...). This pattern often tricks students because there is no constant difference. You must recognize prime numbers instantly by sight.

sections.title: Squares and Cubes Series
sections.content: The terms are perfect squares (1, 4, 9, 16, 25...) or perfect cubes (1, 8, 27, 64, 125...). Recognizing these requires memorizing squares up to 30 and cubes up to 15.

sections.title: Even and Odd Number Series
sections.content: A straightforward sequence where numbers are consecutive even numbers (2, 4, 6, 8) or odd numbers (1, 3, 5, 7), sometimes with a constant added or subtracted.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not checking for prime numbers first and wasting time finding differences. 2. Calculation errors in basic subtraction while finding gaps. 3. Not memorizing squares and cubes, leading to slow identification.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 Number Series relies on basic arithmetic gaps, prime numbers, squares, and cubes. The first step is always to look at the rate of growth: if it's slow, check the differences. If it's recognizable, check primes/squares.

tricks.title: The First Step (Gap Check)
tricks.explanation: If the numbers are increasing gradually, always write down the difference between consecutive terms first.
tricks.example: Series: 5, 9, 14, 20. Differences: +4, +5, +6. Next difference is +7. Next term = 27.

tricks.title: Prime Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: If the differences seem random (e.g., +1, +2, +2, +4) but the numbers themselves are non-divisible, check if they are prime.
tricks.example: Series: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13. The next term is the next prime, which is 17.

tricks.title: Square/Cube Proximity Test
tricks.explanation: If the numbers look familiar but slightly off, see if they are close to a perfect square or cube.

tricks.title: Multiples of Constant
tricks.explanation: Check if the difference is a multiple of a constant number.
tricks.example: Series: 10, 15, 25, 40. Differences: 5, 10, 15. Next difference is 20. Next term = 60.

tricks.title: The Zero Start
tricks.explanation: If a series starts with 0, it is highly likely to be a pattern of (n² - n), (n³ - n), or (n² - 1).
